column1: # .github/ledger-secrets.tsv — every job workflow, and whether anything proves
# A job's ledger is everything about it that outlives it: the spec, every
# step's result and error, every job event, and the process log. All four are
# readable by anyone who can read a job, they are copied into backups, and none
# of them is a place a credential can be withdrawn from once it has landed. A
# passphrase-wrapped key counts as a secret; wrapping makes it attackable
# The assertion itself lives in each workflow's own package, where the harness
# that can run that workflow is. This file is the part no package can see:
# whether every workflow has one. api/internal/ledgertest's register test holds
# it to the tree, so a workflow added tomorrow fails until someone has written
# down which of the three answers applies.
#   covered    `test` names the test(s) that run the workflow on the real
#              Runner and JOBS stream and scan all four surfaces. The gate
#              fails if a named test does not exist.
#   typed      every credential the workflow holds is a secret.Value from its
#              store read, mint or derivation to a named, allowlisted exit
#              tests that prove the exit carries it and the ledger does not;
#              `note` says where it is typed and cites any residual still
#              open, in the cross-repo form. The gate fails on a missing
#              note or a named test that does not exist.
#   pending    no assertion yet. `cite` names the issue that will add it, and
#              `test` is empty. This is a gap, recorded — not a pass. None is
#              left (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#825), and the gate keeps it so.
#   no-secret  the workflow handles no credential material. `note` says why.
#              That claim IS the assertion for this workflow, so it is written
#              down or it is not made.

The stop command carries the app id and a delete-volumes flag; the leaf teardown sends AppLeafCmd with only the app id and Remove, and the control-plane leaf directory is deleted without being read.

The resolved compose is a secret.Value from appsecret.Resolve to deployCommand, its one exit into AppDeployCmd; the leaf key is one from mesh.PrepareAppLeaf to deliverLeaf, destroyed on every outcome. The spec carries no credential. Open: the deploy ack text, geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#749.

The resolved compose is a secret.Value from appsecret.Resolve to deployCommand, its one exit into AppDeployCmd; the leaf key is one from mesh.PrepareAppLeaf to deliverLeaf, destroyed on every outcome. The submitted compose is held in the ComposeStash, never the spec. The spec carries no credential. Open: the deploy ack text, geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#749.

The resolved compose is a secret.Value from appsecret.Resolve to deployCommand, its one exit into AppDeployCmd; the leaf key is one from mesh.PrepareAppLeaf to deliverLeaf, destroyed on every outcome. The spec names the target compose by hash. The spec carries no credential. Open: the deploy ack text, geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#749.
AppStopCmd carries the app id only. Nothing on this path reads a credential, writes one, or asks the agent for one.

The resolved compose is a secret.Value from appsecret.Resolve to deployCommand, its one exit into AppDeployCmd; the leaf key is one from mesh.PrepareAppLeaf to deliverLeaf, destroyed on every outcome. The spec carries no credential. Open: the deploy ack text, geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#749.

The leaf key is a secret.Value from mesh.PrepareAppLeaf to deliverLeaf (AppLeafCmd) and writeKey (its owner-only file, after the node accepts), destroyed on every outcome. The step result carries counts only.

The recovery path leaf key is a secret.Value from mesh.PrepareAppLeaf to deliverLeaf and writeKey, destroyed on every outcome. The status query carries the app id only; the step result carries counts only.

The archive private key is a secret.Value held beside the spec in storage.RestoreSessions, never in it; the spec carries only the session id (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#732). The restore transfer credential is a secret.Value from RestoreEgress.Mint to sendRestoreVolume, its one exit into BackupRestoreVolumeCmd, destroyed when the send returns.

The credential is a secret.Value from bmc.StoredCredential to injectJSONField (the configure command) and ConfigHash; an unreadable one fails the job, the handler and the reconcile closed. The selection fingerprint in the spec, the step log and inventory is a keyed MAC (credmac) under a key derived from the app-secret seed, which no ledger reader holds.
The spec is a node id and a power verb; the power command carries no credential and the agent needs none beyond its bus session.
The spec is a node id and the result is a round-trip time. Nothing on this path reads a credential, writes one, or asks the agent for one.

The PPPoE secret is a secret.Value from the store read to revealState, its one exit into the apply command and the state fingerprint. The fingerprint in the step results and the apply command is a keyed MAC (credmac); the agent's unkeyed ack hash is not compared or recorded.

Upserts the control plane's dns_forward intent through ListIntents, which never joins the PPPoE secret, and submits firewall.apply when it changed. It sends no command of its own and reads no credential.

The WAN password the agent reports is sealed into a secret.Value as the reply is decoded and destroyed when the fetch step returns; its one exit is revealState, into the keyed state fingerprint (credmac). The step results, step logs and change events carry only keyed fingerprints; the agent's unkeyed hash is read only to settle a pre-upgrade intent hash and is never written.
The spec and the command carry a node id and a bool; the compiled intents and their secrets are not read on this path.
Compiles the mesh policy from its intents, none of which holds a pre-auth key or a leaf key; nothing on this path reads or sends one.
Copies pre-auth key metadata only (user, flags, tags); HSPreAuthKey has no field that carries the key itself.
The spec is a node id and a reason string typed by the operator. The command carries no credential, and the agent needs none beyond the bus session it already holds.
The spec is a node id and a bundle digest; the commands carry the bundle id, its URL, signature URL, digest and size. The bundle routes need no credential.
The deploy command's compose names the collector's node key by its path on the node and carries the public CA and the SPKI hash; no private key or token travels.
Decides from the opt-in and recent job history which nodes need a collector deployed or torn down, and submits those jobs. It reads and sends no credential.
The command is AppStopCmd for the collector app; no credential is read or sent.
Stops the local observability supervisor; its configuration holds no credential.
Starts the local observability supervisor; its configuration holds no credential.
Inspects each target by partition UUID (StorageInspectCmd); no key, wrapping or transfer credential is read or sent.
Fans out node.update child jobs; the spec and each child spec carry node ids and a bundle digest, never a credential.
